newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges amicable end to Canada salmon standoff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges amicable end to Canada salmon standoff.

text.p: The White House on Monday urged a peaceful end to a blockade of an Alaskan ferry in British Columbia by Canadian fisherman angered by an unresolved dispute with the United States over salmon fishing.

"We've called upon the Canadian government to enforce the court injunction that's been ordered and continue to hope that both sides can amicably resolve the differences that they've got over maritime issues," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
"We hope it's peacefully resolved and the unneccessary hinderance that has been extended to the ferry passengers ends quickly," he said.

Canadian fisherman, angered by allegations that Alaskan fisherman have taken more than double their normal catch of salmon so far this year, blockaded an Alaskan ferry in the harbor at Prince Rupert, British Columbia, about 1,000 miles (1,600 km) north of Vancouver. The blockade was in its third day on Monday. About 142 passengers were aboard the ferry.
Canada has accused the United States of overfishing Pacific Ocean salmon, while U.S. officials blame Canada for scuttling recent talks aimed at reaching a deal on how to divide this year's catch.
Canadian police were expected to begin on Monday enforcing a court order compelling the fishing boats to allow the ferry to pass.
